content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I know how to read from VM memory using the Network input block by specifying the address you want, but I am having trouble writing data to VM memory. Can you write a flag's state to VM memory? Also, which blocks can be written to VM memory? Any advice would be greatly appreciated. [user_name]

I found the answer after searching on the [company_name] website and included the relevant instructions. It turns out there is no need to write a flag’s state to VM memory on the server, since the client can directly read the state of flags, as well as input and output states, from the server. I hope this information helps anyone else looking to begin with networking for [product_name].

Inputs, outputs, and flags are automatically mapped to VM memory. Here are the addresses for reference: DI VM-Adresse, DQ VM-Adresse, I1 V923.0, Q1 V942.0, ... (continues with all address listings in the original post). These address assignments make it easier to locate and access the correct VM memory locations. Best regards.

A new question from [user_name] has been moved to a dedicated thread with the subject 'Change of addresses of Inputs, outputs and flags in VM memory with [product_name] [version_no]'. Best regards, [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: Initially, users were unsure how to write a flag's state to VM memory in [company_name] [product_name] hardware and which memory blocks could be written. Discussion and documentation clarified that input, output, and flag states are assigned to VM memory automatically and can be read directly, so explicit writing is not needed. Address mappings for these functions were shared, improving understanding of memory access for networking.
analysis.user_expectations: Users hope to be able to write internal flag states to VM memory so other networked devices can read them, and want clear guidance about which parts of memory support writing.
pain_keywords: uncertainty about writing to VM memory
